# SB-1020 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting
Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

## Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during blasting activities in the vicinity of the Ring Rolling area presents inhalation and contamination hazards to personnel and to sensitive process equipment. The blasting media and removed surface material can produce respirable particulates that migrate along airflows created by process ventilation and mobile equipment movement. Exposure can result in respiratory irritation, contamination of machine surfaces, fouling of bearings and seals, and increased fire risk where fines accumulate on hot surfaces or electrical enclosures. Secondary hazards include the potential for dust to enter bearing housings and tooling interfaces, increasing wear and risking seizure if not controlled.

Background: Blasting is required for surface preparation on cast and forged components prior to machining and rolling operations. The combination of blasting residue and existing process dust creates a mixed particulate field that behaves differently than a single-source dust. This bulletin focuses on controls to reduce airborne particulate migration into the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill EQ-P1-L2-RR01 and immediate work areas, and to ensure maintenance tasks that expose internal interfaces include dust control measures.

Step rationale: Controls emphasize source containment, controlled capture, personal protection, and housekeeping to prevent dust deposition in critical machine areas. Where service access requires removal of covers or exposure of lubrication points, procedural controls mitigate the risk of particulate ingress to bearings, mandrels, clamps and tooling interfaces.

## Affected equipment
- Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) located on P1-L2.
- Surrounding support zones where blasting is performed and where airflow paths can reach the equipment.
- Portable process auxiliary equipment that transfers parts between blasting stations and the mill.

The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m.

Technicians who perform mandrel installation, clamp adjustment, seal replacement, or bearing service on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 are considered affected personnel and must follow the controls below.

Related documents: ECN-2026-009, SOP-P1-L2-03, SOP-P1-L2-05

## Required controls
Controls are grouped by priority: source control, capture and containment, administrative procedures, personal protective equipment, and verification records.

- Source control: Coordinate blasting schedules to avoid performing abrasive blasting immediately upwind or in direct airflow paths toward EQ-P1-L2-RR01. When blasting is required near the line, use contained blasting booths or portable enclosures with negative pressure capture to prevent fugitive dust migration into the mill area. Exhaust from blasting containments must be filtered before release to the plant environment as described in ECN-2026-009.

- Capture and containment at the mill: When EQ-P1-L2-RR01 is idle for maintenance that exposes internal assemblies, install temporary sealed covers over exposed openings and apply local extraction at the access point to prevent dust ingress. Use cleanable covers that do not shed fibers. Avoid using permeable cloth as a final barrier where particulate control is required.

- Administrative procedures: Work planning for blasting and for maintenance on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 must be coordinated through line supervision. All blasting work orders that could affect P1-L2 must reference SOP-P1-L2-03 and SOP-P1-L2-05. Maintenance work that requires mandrel removal or clamp bolt access must include pre-task hazard assessment noting potential dust exposure and specifying isolation and cleaning steps prior to reassembly.

- Personal protective equipment: Personnel working near blasting operations or during cleanup shall wear approved respiratory protection and eye protection as required by site PPE policy. Respiratory selection and fit must be consistent with SOP-P1-L2-05 and the applicable exposure assessment referenced in ECN-2026-009.

- Housekeeping: Implement targeted cleaning of handrails, control panels, junction boxes, and mill housings at regular intervals determined by local supervision and recorded in the maintenance log. Use vacuum capture designed for industrial dusts rather than compressed air for cleaning machine surfaces.

- Reassembly and torque control: After any activity that could result in dust ingress into clamps or mandrel interfaces, clean mating surfaces using approved non-shedding wipes and re-lubricate per SOP-P1-L2-03. Reinstall mandrel clamp bolts and apply the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m.

Examples: A blasting job performed at the adjacent prep area created visible dust migration toward the mill during a shift change. Corrective practice was to delay blasting until after completion of scheduled mandrel changeout and to use a portable enclosure with filtered exhaust during all subsequent near-line blasting operations. Another example: a bearing housing was found to contain abrasive fines after an unscheduled blast; the maintenance team quarantined the assembly, performed controlled disassembly within a downdraft booth, replaced contaminated lubricant, and documented actions in the maintenance record as required below.

## Records to keep
- Blast job coordination records that reference SOP-P1-L2-03 and SOP-P1-L2-05 and note measures taken to protect P1-L2 equipment. Retain in the line coordination folder and attach to the work order record.
- Maintenance reports for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 that document cleaning steps performed, verification of sealing measures, and confirmation that the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m was applied during reassembly. Include technician initials and supervisor approval.
- Air capture and filter maintenance logs for any temporary enclosures used during blasting activities, referenced to ECN-2026-009.
- Incident and observation reports related to dust migration or contamination near EQ-P1-L2-RR01. Enter into the plant safety database and notify line management.

Verification: Supervision shall inspect the equipment area after blasting events and before restarting EQ-P1-L2-RR01. Verification includes visual inspection for dust accumulation on control surfaces and key interfaces, review of the maintenance report for torque confirmation, and spot checks of temporary enclosures.

## Effective date
Effective upon release Rev A. All blasting and maintenance planning that could affect P1-L2 shall implement the controls above and reference ECN-2026-009, SOP-P1-L2-03, SOP-P1-L2-05 for detailed procedures.
